ideas.pitch: An autonomous agent that reads web-based compliance documents and orchestrates multi-step form submissions while running pre-deployment risk checks through BPMN workflows.
ideas.title: Anakin-BPMN Risk Auditor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the multi-step reasoning and web-browsing capabilities explicitly requested in the hackathon prompt while employing advanced agent governance patterns.

ideas.pitch: A training-free semantic router that sits in front of an Anakin Forge web-scraping agent, continuously optimizing its task routing via LLM-judge writebacks and exemplar indexing.
ideas.title: Self-Improving Semantic Router for Web Agents
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on genuinely hard engineering by solving the routing overhead for autonomous agents that must quickly decide whether to scrape, click, or reason.

ideas.pitch: Two autonomous browser agents play opposing roles—one acts as a chaotic user trying to break a target web application, and the other acts as an auditing agent discovering edge cases and UI flaws.
ideas.title: Adversarial UI Tester Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Applies a proven winning pattern of multi-agent adversarial interaction to real web browsing tasks, directly fitting the requirement for agents that take real actions without human clicks.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous agent leveraging Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to securely read live clinical portals, compare options, and execute multi-step administrative workflows end-to-end.
ideas.title: MCP Federated Medical Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Demonstrates enterprise-grade agent architecture with strict context isolation, which stands out among basic wrapper chatbots in a web-and-action focused hackathon.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight web navigation agent integrated with efficient reasoning loops to drastically cut down token usage and latency when browsing multi-page enterprise dashboards.
ideas.title: Hyper-Efficient Reasoning Web Navigator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Tackles the core bottleneck of autonomous web agents—token cost and reasoning latency—which judges evaluating practical utility will immediately value.
